subject: Renewal: Dedicated capacity amendment — request to increase 8→16 GPUs and monthly commit
body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Irwin <sam.irwin@avatech.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal prep — proposal to expand Dedicated capacity (8→16 GPUs)

Sam —

As we start the renewal conversation for Ava Tech (thanks again for the partnership), wanted to put a concrete proposal on the table to make sure capacity aligns with your Q2 product roadmap. At contract renewal (current term ends 2026-03-31) you asked about scaling the Dedicated pool from the current 8 GPUs to 16 GPUs and increasing the monthly reserved commit.

High-level ask / proposal:
- Increase reserved GPUs: 8 → 16 (same instance type: A100-like equivalent in our Dedicated pool)
- Monthly commit: current: 8 GPU-hours equivalent commit; proposed new commit: 16 GPU-hours equivalent (we can convert to $/month as part of the amendment)
- Throughput guarantee: target baseline throughput of ~1.6M tokens/day (approx. doubling from current profiles) with a 99.9% availability SLA for the reserved pool
- Rollout: canonical start on renewal effective date, with an option for a 30-day phased ramp (8→12→16) if Ava prefers to smooth spend

Can you confirm that this aligns with your procurement timeline? If so I’ll loop in Rishi to confirm provisioning lead times and Monica to put the updated amendment together.

Thanks —
Marissa
-----
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sam Irwin <sam.irwin@avatech.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@avatech.io>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 10:02:14 -0500
Subject: Re: Renewal prep — proposal to expand Dedicated capacity (8→16 GPUs)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for outlining. Ava Tech is interested in moving to 16 GPUs at renewal but we have two questions before we commit:
1) Can you share the expected delta in monthly spend (line-item) and the effective per-GPU discounted rate if we commit to 12-month term?
2) What is the provisioning lead time? Our infra team has a migration window planned for mid-April, so we need the extra capacity available by then.

Procurement: I’ve cc'd our procurement mailbox; they’ll expect a formal amendment and an invoice schedule.

—Sam
Sam Irwin
Head of Platform Engineering, Ava Tech
sam.irwin@avatech.io

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sam Irwin <sam.irwin@avatech.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal prep — proposal to expand Dedicated capacity (8→16 GPUs)

Hi Sam —

We can support the 8→16 GPU expansion, here's what to expect from the infra side: 
- Provisioning lead time: baseline 3–4 weeks after amendment signature for Dedicated pool capacity to be reserved and tested in your region (US West). If you opt for a phased ramp we can start reserving capacity earlier for the first tranche.
- Throughput guidance: based on your current usage profile (avg seq len, concurrency), we estimate each GPU will deliver ~120–140k tokens/hour under optimized batching. Doubling GPUs should give ~2x throughput for most steady-state workloads; see attached throughput_calc_avatech.xlsx for scenario modeling.
- SLA/availability: we can offer 99.9% uptime on the reserved pool and a 30-minute failover to a compatible fallback model (hosted tier) if we detect capacity issues during maintenance windows.
- Operational notes: we recommend enabling prefix KV caching and a 1-week canary with production traffic shadowing before switching write traffic to the larger pool.

Attachments: throughput_calc_avatech.xlsx (spreadsheet with per-GPU throughput and cost scenarios)

If procurement needs lead time guarantees in writing, we can add a provisioning timeline clause in the amendment.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Serving Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

From: Sam Irwin <sam.irwin@avatech.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@avatech.io>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:27:30 -0500
Subject: Re: Renewal prep — proposal to expand Dedicated capacity (8→16 GPUs)

Appreciate the detail, Rishi. A couple follow-ups: 
- Phased ramp: Ava would prefer a 2-step ramp (effective 2026-04-01 start: 8→12; 2026-04-15: 12→16). Will you be able to guarantee the 12 GPU tranche by 4/1?
- Pricing elasticity: would it be possible to lock in a slightly lower rate if we commit to a 24-month term instead of 12? We’re evaluating a longer-term commit if the price delta is material.

Procurement will need the amendment + a DocuSign link and the invoice schedule. Can Marissa and Monica share a redline-friendly amendment by next week?

Thanks,
Sam

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Sam Irwin <sam.irwin@avatech.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 09:03:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal prep — proposal to expand Dedicated capacity (8→16 GPUs)

Sam —

We can accommodate the phased ramp you outlined. Confirmations: 
- We will reserve the initial 4-GPU uplift (to 12) to be available by 2026-04-01 and the final tranche to reach 16 by 2026-04-15, contingent on amendment signature by 2026-03-10 to hit procurement timelines. 
- Pricing: Marissa will include both 12-month and 24-month commit tiers in the amendment. The 24-month tier includes an additional 7% volume discount on the GPU-hour rate.
- Billing start: billing for incremental reserve will align to the date the tranche is provisioned (we can also start billing on the renewal effective date at your preference).

I’ll attach a proposal doc and the amendment draft for redlines next week.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Irwin <sam.irwin@avatech.io>, Procurement Team <procurement@avatech.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2026 14:22:05 -0800
Subject: Renewal amendment: 8→16 GPUs (redline-ready)

Sam / Procurement team —

Attached is the redline-ready amendment (Redwood_Dedicated_Amendment_v2.pdf) reflecting the options we discussed:
- Option A: 12-month term, immediate 8→16 upgrade effective on the renewal date (2026-04-01). Monthly committed spend: $XX,XXX (line items included in PDF).
- Option B: 24-month term, immediate 8→16 upgrade with 7% volume discount. Monthly committed spend: $YY,YYY.
- Option C: Phased ramp (8→12 on 2026-04-01; 12→16 on 2026-04-15) — billing aligns to tranche provisioning date.

Callouts:
- Provisioning clause: we added a 4-week provisioning lead time guarantee and a credit schedule in case we miss the committed availability SLA for the reserved pool.
- Throughput appendix: references throughput_calc_avatech.xlsx for expected tokens/day and target batch sizing recommendations.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Procurement picks Option A/B/C and returns a redline by EOD 2026-03-05.
2) We post the signed amendment via DocuSign (link included) and target signature by 2026-03-10 to meet the provisioning cadence.
3) Rishi’s team performs a 1-week canary starting 2026-03-25 (shadow traffic) before routing live traffic.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Amendment_v2.pdf, throughput_calc_avatech.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.
Marissa

From: Sam Irwin <sam.irwin@avatech.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@avatech.io>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2026 17:42:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Renewal amendment: 8→16 GPUs (redline-ready)

Marissa —

Thanks for the amendment. Procurement wants Option C (phased ramp). Two small asks before signature: 
1) Can the billing for the first tranche (8→12) start on 2026-04-01 even if the tranche completes a late provisioning window (i.e., we accept billing upon tranche activation but want explicit language that the tranche will be available by 4/01 or credits apply)?
2) Please set the DocuSign to bill net-45.

If those two items are included I’ll route to legal and procurement for signing today. Once signed we’ll expect the reserved capacity to be scheduled per Monica/Rishi’s notes.

—Sam
Sam Irwin
Head of Platform Engineering, Ava Tech

[Attachment stubs referenced above: Redwood_Dedicated_Amendment_v2.pdf (application/pdf), throughput_calc_avatech.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
